chapters.title: Business Hours Calendars
chapters.subtitle: Define when you are open, once

steps.text: A business hours calendar says when you are open. This video shows why it exists, where a calendar is used, how to create one with a weekly schedule and holidays, and the rules worth knowing.

chapters.title: Why business hours
chapters.subtitle: One definition of open and closed

steps.text: Callers expect a different answer after hours. A queue that rings agents who have gone home, or a dialer that calls customers at night, wastes time and annoys people.
Without a shared definition, each queue, phone menu and campaign needs its own idea of open, and they drift apart when the schedule changes.
A business hours calendar is that shared definition. Change it once, and everything that uses it follows.
It handles the weekly schedule, a time zone, and the holidays when you are closed all day.

chapters.title: Where a calendar is used
chapters.subtitle: Queues, entry points, the dialer and automated texts

steps.text: A queue uses a calendar to hold or overflow callers while you are closed.
An inbound entry point uses it to pick the closed action: voicemail, overflow, or reject.
A dialer profile uses it as the outbound calling window, checked in the contact's own time zone.
An automatic activity load uses it, so that AI follow-up messages are only sent while you are open.
Open Interaction Center, Management, Business hours. Click Add calendar.
Enter a Name, such as Support hours, and an optional Description.
Pick the Time zone the hours are written in. When it is empty, the hours are in UTC
In Weekly schedule, tick Open for each open day, and set From and To. A new calendar starts with Monday to Friday, nine to five.
Close Friday afternoon early by changing its To time, and tick Open on Saturday for a short morning shift.
In Holidays, enter one date per line, in the form year, month, day. The calendar is closed all day on those dates.
Leave Enabled ticked, and click Save. The calendar is listed, and can now be picked on queues, entry points and dialer profiles.
The To time is exclusive. Nine to five closes at exactly five o'clock.
The same From and To time means open for twenty-four hours.
A To time earlier than the From time runs past midnight, for example ten at night to six in the morning.
Holiday lines that are not valid dates are ignored, so check the list after you save. And a disabled calendar never closes anything: every queue that uses it is treated as always open.

chapters.title: Use cases
chapters.subtitle: What a calendar does for you

steps.text: A support team opens a queue from eight to six on weekdays. After hours, callers reach voicemail instead of a ringing phone.
A sales team calls from nine to five in the customer's time zone, so a customer in another time zone is never called before breakfast.
Holidays are added once, and every queue, menu and campaign that uses the calendar is closed that day.
A team that sends AI follow-up texts keeps them inside opening hours, so nobody is texted at night.
Define your opening hours once, with their time zone and holidays, and let queues, phone menus, the dialer and automated texts follow them. Thanks for watching.
